title: Maintenance Pendente Lite and Expenses — Section 24 HMA

content.overview: Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides interim maintenance and expenses of the proceeding. Where either spouse has no independent income sufficient for support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, the Court may order the other to pay those expenses and a monthly sum during the proceeding, having regard to both incomes. The application is to be disposed of, as far as possible, within sixty days of service of notice.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Pending HMA proceeding? (2) No independent income sufficient for support + expenses? (3) Either spouse may apply? (4) Quantum by both incomes? (5) Distinct from s. 25?
content.study:
Section 24 is the interim-maintenance provision of the HMA.

Where in any proceeding under the Act either spouse has no independent income sufficient for support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, the Court may order the respondent to pay the expenses of the proceeding and a monthly sum during the proceeding, having regard to both parties’ incomes.

Proviso (2001): dispose of the application, as far as possible, within sixty days of service of notice.

Key features: available in any HMA proceeding; gender-neutral; quantum discretionary guided by both incomes; operates only pendente lite.

Distinct from permanent alimony under s. 25 and from maintenance under CrPC s. 125 / BNSS s. 144 and HAMA. Courts avoid double recovery for the same period.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Trigger and relief
sections.body: Pending HMA proceeding; applicant lacks sufficient independent income; relief = litigation expenses + monthly sum during the proceeding.

sections.heading: Gender-neutral
sections.body: Either wife or husband may apply if the income test is met.

sections.heading: Quantum
sections.body: Such sum as appears reasonable having regard to the incomes of both parties.

sections.heading: Sixty-day proviso
sections.body: Application to be disposed of, as far as possible, within sixty days of service of notice.

sections.heading: Contrast with s. 25
sections.body: s. 24 is interim only; permanent provision is under s. 25 at or after the decree.

hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, but courts adjust quantum to avoid double recovery for the same period.

distinctions.title: s. 24 (interim) vs s. 25 (permanent)
distinctions.right: At or after any decree; may last for life of applicant subject to variation.

rows.right: Gross or periodical sum; may be secured by charge.
Term not exceeding life of applicant (subject to variation).

misconceptions.trap: Only the wife can claim under s. 24.
misconceptions.correction: Either spouse may apply; the provision is gender-neutral.

misconceptions.trap: Section 24 is the same as permanent alimony under s. 25.
misconceptions.correction: Section 24 is strictly interim; permanent provision is under s. 25.
